calls.head: Philadelphia rolls four lines; New Jersey leans on its top six
calls.body: On depth, Philadelphia sits 3rd of 32, at the deep end of the scale. New Jersey is 31st, at the top-heavy end.
calls.call: Philadelphia spreads its forward ice time deeper down the lineup than New Jersey.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On bottom-six share of forward ice time, Philadelphia had 42% and New Jersey 39%. Coming in, Philadelphia was at 43% and New Jersey at 40%.

calls.head: Philadelphia hits; New Jersey mostly doesn’t
calls.body: On physicality, Philadelphia sits 4th of 32, at the bruising end of the scale. New Jersey is 31st, at the finesse end.
calls.call: Philadelphia hits more than New Jersey in the close stretches of the game.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On hit score in close games (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average), Philadelphia had 124 and New Jersey 88. Coming in, Philadelphia was at 116 and New Jersey at 85.

NJD.head: We gave New Jersey a 60% chance, and New Jersey delivered.

PHI.head: We gave Philadelphia only a 40% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Philadelphia was kept to the outside
surprises.body: Philadelphia needed 24.4 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 15.7 and a league average of 15.9. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: Philadelphia tried a different line
surprises.body: M. Michkov, N. Cates, T. Foerster played 7:52 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Philadelphia’s usual lines.
